name: RNIT AI Solutions Ltd
tagline: Government-scale facial-recognition SaaS microcap with genuine YoY growth and improving ROCE (20.2%), but a rich ~61x multiple, a post-NCLT-resolution corporate history, two rapid dilutive capital raises, and near-total government-customer concentration
business_overview: RNIT AI Solutions describes itself as the largest AI-based Facial Recognition System (FRS) SaaS player serving the Indian government sector, claiming 3 billion+ identity verifications processed across 300+ government departments, now expanded to 9 states/UTs (2026 wins include Goa, Lakshadweep, Meghalaya). Listed on BSE (517286) under the legacy name Autopal Industries Ltd; this pass confirms the company emerged from an NCLT-approved insolvency Resolution Plan, with the RNIT AI business injected post-resolution — FY24 (pre-resolution) revenue was effectively nil per screener.in, and FY25 is the first real operating year. This is a first-time open-screen deep dive; there is no dedicated ValuePickr thread; assessment is web/news + screener.in + old-project baseline.

FY25 ~Rs32cr → FY26 ~Rs52cr; FY24 (pre-NCLT-resolution) was effectively nil — real operating history is only ~2 years
~0.13 (total debt ~Rs18cr vs net worth ~Rs139cr) — CORRECTED this pass; the prior ~5.0x figure was stale/mis-scaled against a much smaller pre-capital-raise equity base

fundamentals_narrative: The core growth-plus-margin story holds up and has improved on some dimensions since the last pass: ROCE rose to ~20.2% (from ~12.2%), OPM structurally rose from 32% (FY25) to 40% (FY26), and revenue/PAT growth (+62%/+67% FY26) remains real, not just off a tiny base — quarterly revenue has grown YoY in every comparable quarter through FY26 and into Q1 FY27. But this pass surfaced a materially more complex picture than the earlier summary: (1) the listed entity (BSE 517286, legacy name Autopal Industries Ltd) emerged from an NCLT-approved insolvency Resolution Plan, with the RNIT AI business injected afterward — FY24 revenue was effectively nil, so real operating history is only ~2 years; (2) the company raised ~Rs47cr via two preferential allotments five months apart (Nov 2025 ~Rs20.83cr, Mar 2026 ~Rs26.33cr) toward a targeted Rs50cr programme, and promoter holding swung from 52.28% (Jun 2024) to 73.74% (Sep 2025, post-resolution new promoter/investor group) to 67.42% (Mar 2026) as those raises diluted the base; (3) working-capital days are elevated (debtor days 146, WC days 195), consistent with a recurring Q4-heavy/Q1-trough quarterly pattern tied to government payment cycles (Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs8.20cr was down ~53% sequentially from Q4 FY26's Rs17.62cr, though still +31% YoY); (4) the old Debt/Equity figure of ~5.0x in the prior write-up appears stale or mis-scaled — against the current balance sheet (net worth ~Rs139cr, debt ~Rs18cr) leverage is actually low, ~0.13x, corrected this pass. Implied P/E is still rich at ~61x. A genuine new fact this pass: an August 2026 Master Development Services Agreement with 1FC Technology is the company's first disclosed step into FinTech/WealthTech/InsurTech, a partial mitigant to the otherwise near-total government-customer concentration.

verdict_headline: Growth and ROCE genuinely improved and a real new fintech-diversification commitment landed, but a rich multiple, a post-NCLT-resolution corporate history and rapid dilutive capital raises keep conviction at Medium
verdict_reasoning: four_box score is 3.0 (tailwind=yes, tam=yes, moat=yes on the government-FRS-SaaS niche; valuation=no at ~61x against a still-thin 2-year operating history) — clears the ≥3.0 bar, so 10x-in-2-3-years is permitted per the quickref decision table; conviction is set separately

New facts this pass are a genuine mix: ROCE improved to ~20.2% (from ~12.2%) and OPM to 40% (from 32%), and the Aug 2026 1FC Technology agreement is a real, evidenced diversification beyond government customers — but the company's real operating history is only ~2 years (it emerged from an NCLT-approved insolvency Resolution Plan; FY24 revenue was effectively nil) and it has raised ~Rs47cr via two preferential allotments five months apart, with promoter holding swinging 52.28%→73.74%→67.42% over that period

No red flag: none of the enumerated hard triggers (negative net worth, going concern, SEBI/fraud order, auditor resignation, promoter-holding collapse) are confirmed — the promoter-holding swing looks dilution-driven, not a collapse — so red_flag_tier stays none, but the resolution-plan history and rapid capital raises are flagged prominently as context a future pass should keep tracking

Conviction held at Medium: the fundamental improvement (ROCE, margin, real new-vertical diversification) is real, but a ~61x multiple, elevated working capital (146/195 days), near-total government concentration, and the thin 2-year post-resolution operating history all argue against upgrading further without independent (ValuePickr-level) scrutiny
